negative_controls.description: A mixed-cluster random caucus of the same size must not be flagged as an echo chamber. Detector uses spread vs random baseline, not the formation label.
Replace one cited turn with a turn from another group; report-up fidelity must FAIL.
Drop one member's cited turn; report-up fidelity must FAIL.
If affinity did not fire, the random negative control would be vacuously silent. Detector-control requires the planted like-minded caucus to fire.

question_or_target: Implement tools/council/topology/committee.py partitioning a council into standing committees and ad-hoc caucuses that deliberate separately and report up. Falsifiable question: does a caucus formed from like-minded participants produce an echo chamber, measured as reduced position spread relative to a randomly formed caucus of the same size?

residual_unknowns.claim: Positions are numeric fixtures (two clusters), not live model outputs. The echo-chamber result is therefore a composition effect of affinity grouping, which is the catalog's falsifiable question, not a claim about LLM sycophancy.
residual_unknowns.settling_experiment: Re-run compare_affinity_vs_random with participant adapters once IMP-0265 seating is on disk.

residual_unknowns.claim: Turns are recorded by RecordingKernel inside this module, not by tools/council/kernel.py (IMP-0264 is absent here). The topology port is execute_turn; a production kernel can replace the double without changing committee.py's call sites.
ECHO_CHAMBER_MAX_RATIO=0.5 is a documented constant, not fitted on a large corpus. The measured affinity/baseline ratio was 0.0493, so the qualitative result is not threshold-fragile on this roster.
